Nora (Acct Exec): Heads up — OmegaCorp POC failing with 413 when they send a single JSON body containing a base64 PDF bundle. They say its ~11MB raw and grows to ~14.5MB base64. Any quick unblock?

Sam (SalesEng): Which endpoint did they call? embeddings or our file ingest path?

Nora (Acct Exec): /v1/embeddings. Example they sent (redacted):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"embed-large","input":"<base64-pdf-zip>"}'
```

Client gets HTTP/1.1 413 and sometimes an empty response body. No client-side request-id.

upload-bot: gateway error: 413, client=172.20.5.14, server=api.redwood.ai, request="POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1", upstream="http://upstream:8080/"

Rina (Support): Base64 expansion ~33% is normal. 11MB -> ~14.6MB checks out. Short-term unblocks: 1) use presigned S3 PUT and pass us URL, 2) switch to binary upload (application/octet-stream) to avoid base64, or 3) split into smaller chunks.

Omar (Edge Eng): Our edge/nginx default max_body_size is 10M for public tenants. We can do a tenant-scoped increase for short windows, but needs Ops approval and risk review. Also corporate proxies between them and our edge might abort earlier than our limit.

Leela (Security): Presigned S3 is usually fine for enterprise; if their compliance team forbids third-party storage, they sometimes want a direct multipart/form-data upload into our ingest service. We should offer an encrypted presign workflow (SSE-KMS) to ease controls.

Sam (SalesEng): For immediate POC I suggest this flow: 1) provide presigned PUT (S3) with SSE-KMS option, 2) ask them to PUT binary gzipped bundle (not base64) to presigned URL, 3) call /v1/embeddings with {"input_url":"s3://...","model":"embed-large"}. That avoids edge body limits and base64 overhead.

Rina (Support): If they're blocked from using S3, fallback: multipart client-side split into <8MB pieces, POST each to embeddings and aggregate vectors client-side (mean or weighted). We'll give sample scripts.

Omar (Edge Eng): If customer insists on single POST to our API, we can open a temporary exception: raise max_body_size to 25M for their tenant and restrict by src CIDR. Ops will need justification + TTL. Also note larger bodies increase logging and WAF inspection costs.

Nora (Acct Exec): Customer asked if larger uploads affect pricing. Quick answer?

Rina (Support): Bandwidth increases slightly. If we end up tokenizing large text or reprocessing it (e.g., completions), tokens matter. For embeddings only, cost is based on embedding units; upload size itself isn't billed per token, but network egress and storage are factors. For POC, we absorb small anomalies.

Sam (SalesEng): We should offer a small how-to and code snippet. Drafting now.

Leela (Security): Also offer a short data handling statement they can send to their security team: short bullets about presigned flow, SSE-KMS, access controls, retention policy. I can draft.

Rina (Support): Quick client example for presign flow:

```
# client: PUT binary gzipped bundle to presigned URL
curl -X PUT "<presigned-url>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @bundle.zip.gz

# then call embeddings with pointer
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"embed-large","input_url":"s3://omega-bucket/bundle.zip.gz"}'
```

Sam (SalesEng): If we need an SDK snippet I can attach node/python examples. Also recommend gzipping before upload to reduce size.

Omar (Edge Eng): FYI if they report 413 but our gateway logs don't show a corresponding request-id, it's likely their corporate proxy rejecting before it hits us. Ask them to curl with -v and capture the full response headers.

Nora (Acct Exec): I'll send the presign + security note to their infra lead and ask for the proxy logs. I'll request permission for the temporary gateway increase as a fallback.

Leela (Security): I'll draft the one-pager for security and include SSE-KMS headers example and retention policy line items.

Rina (Support): Will add a small client-side chunking script and an example manifest format for reassembly/aggregation.

Sam (SalesEng): Marking action items: Nora to reach out to Omega infra; Sam will prepare SDK snippets; Leela will write the security note; Omar will standby for gateway exception ticket.

Nora (Acct Exec): Thanks all. I'll update when I hear back. :white_check_mark:
